changes.to:
Frontend renders raw canonical message part JSON as plain text in chat bubbles at turn end.

## Observed
At the start of the assistant turn, raw JSON like this leaks into the chat UI:



This appears to be the raw canonical message parts array (thinking + tool_call) being displayed instead of being parsed and rendered properly by the frontend message renderer.

## Screenshots
- @uploads/IMG_8326.png — shows raw JSON at top of assistant response after user asks "What model are you ?"
- @uploads/IMG_8327.png — shows same raw JSON plus tool result sections below

## Expected
Thinking parts should render as expandable thinking blocks (or be hidden). Tool calls should render as compact tool-call pills/blocks. Raw JSON should never be visible to the user.

## Suspected area
Frontend message rendering pipeline — likely the message-to-React rendering path is falling through to a raw text display when it encounters parts it doesn't know how to render, or the message payload is being stringified and appended as text.

## Related
- oqto-dnj4 — model mismatch (same screenshots show both bugs)

changes.to:
Selected model on frontend is not respected by Pi - Pi starts with a different model than what the user selected.

## Fresh evidence (2026-05-10)
User has "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5" selected in the frontend model picker (bottom bar shows "fhgenie-preview" / "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5"), but when asked "What model are you ?", Pi reports it is running as gpt-5.3-codex (Azure Foundry) with Model ID Foundry-Codex/gpt-5.3-codex.

This is a live regression visible in production.

## Screenshots
- uploads/IMG_8326.png — model selector shows MiniMax-M2.5, user asks "What model are you ?"
- uploads/IMG_8327.png — Pi tool result replies "I am running as gpt-5.3-codex (Azure Foundry)"

## Suspected area
- Frontend model selection state not being included in the prompt command sent to runner
- Runner not passing model override to Pi startup
- Pi defaulting to a different model because OQTO_MODEL or equivalent env var is not set correctly

## Related
- oqto-xv6t — raw markdown leaking (same screenshots show both bugs)

changes.to:
Goal
Add a secure secret submission and use flow for RPC clients that routes secrets from client to owning runner and into runner-local kyz, without exposing secret values to agent/model transcripts, chat history, or tool logs.

Why
- Pi core cannot be changed; solution must be extension + Oqto platform.
- RPC clients need parity with TUI secure secret workflows.
- Future remote runners require locality: secret resolution/injection should happen on runner host.

Architecture
- Data path (secret bytes): Client -> Backend -> Runner -> kyz (local on runner host)
- Control path (metadata only): extension/agent commands and status events
- Secret values must never flow through chat message content, tool args shown to model, or persisted history.

Scope
1) Canonical RPC command additions (agent/files/ws channel as appropriate)
   - secret.submit (runner-routed)
   - secret.submit_status / command_response (metadata only)
   Payload (submit):
   - request_id (uuid)
   - session_id (platform session)
   - workspace_path (optional but preferred)
   - service, key
   - value (sensitive payload)
   - expires_at (short TTL)
   - origin metadata (client build/user id/device id)

2) Backend relay hardening
   - Route sensitive command only to owning runner of session/workspace.
   - Mark payload as sensitive in tracing pipeline:
     - no structured logs of value
     - no websocket debug echo of value
     - no persistence in hstry/oqto-log
   - Enforce max payload size and required fields.

3) Runner secure handling
   - Accept secret.submit only from authenticated backend channel.
   - Validate request_id TTL and replay window (request_id dedup cache).
   - Forward value to local kyz endpoint/CLI stdin path without shell interpolation.
   - Immediately zero/drop in-memory buffers post-use where practical.
   - Return success/failure + denial code (no value in error text).

4) Policy/authorization checks
   - Session/workspace ownership check (user cannot submit to foreign runner/session).
   - Optional allowlist for service/key namespaces per workspace/org policy.
   - Deny with explicit taxonomy: unauthorized, expired, replay, invalid_payload, out_of_scope, kyz_unavailable.

5) Audit events (non-sensitive)
   - Emit metadata-only audit records:
     - ts, user_id, session_id, runner_id, workspace, service/key, request_id, outcome, denial_code
   - Never include secret value or derived encodings.

6) Extension integration contract (pi-kyz)
   - RPC mode: /kyz-set must not solicit plaintext in chat.
   - Extension triggers secure client flow and awaits submit_status.
   - TUI mode can continue local masked input path.

7) Remote-runner readiness
   - Ensure backend always routes to runner-local kyz; no backend-global secret store fallback.
   - Define failure behavior when runner offline (queued? reject?). Prefer explicit reject with retry guidance.

Security requirements
- No value in logs (backend/runner/frontend), telemetry, traces, or persisted events.
- No value in command previews/tool output shown to LLM.
- No shell command interpolation containing secret value.
- Replay + expiry enforcement mandatory.
- Request correlation via request_id only.

Testing
A) Unit
- Payload redaction tests in backend logging path.
- Replay/expiry checks in runner.
- Ownership/authorization checks.

B) Integration
- End-to-end RPC submit success: secret appears in kyz on runner host.
- Verify no secret appears in:
  - browser console
  - backend logs
  - runner logs
  - hstry/oqto-log messages/events
- Denial-path tests: expired, replayed, unauthorized, malformed.

C) E2E (agent-browser)
- Trigger /kyz-set in RPC client flow.
- Complete secure form/input on client.
- Confirm agent receives only success message.
- Use secret via kyz exec/pipe path successfully.

Acceptance criteria
1. RPC client can set secret via client->runner->kyz with no transcript exposure.
2. Secret value is absent from all logs/history/events by automated checks.
3. Replay and expiry protections are enforced.
4. Ownership checks prevent cross-session/workspace misuse.
5. Works with remote runner topology (runner-local kyz only).

Out of scope
- Pi core changes.
- Full centralized secret broker replacing kyz.
- Bulk secret replication to runner hosts.

changes.to:
## Problem
Any sandboxed agent can read every session transcript across ALL workspaces (and other harnesses) regardless of profile. This violates the oqto-log access model ("scope derived from oqto-sandbox read permissions; no raw cross-workspace reads").

## Evidence (backend/crates/oqto-sandbox/src/config.rs)
- minimal: deny_read = ssh/gnupg/aws/systemctl only; ~/.pi unrestricted.
- development (default): ~/.pi, ~/.claude, ~/.local/share/claude, ~/.codex, ~/.local/share/codex all in allow_write (=> readable). lines ~466-475.
- strict: ~/.pi in allow_write (line ~548); deny_read covers ~/.config but not session dirs.
- spawn.rs: `_workspace: &Path` param is UNUSED (lines 26, 76) -> zero per-workspace session-dir scoping exists.

Net: an agent in workspace A can read `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--{other_workspace}--/*.jsonl` for every other project, plus Claude/Codex history. A duckdb one-liner slurps the entire corpus.

## Root cause
Harnesses must WRITE their own session files (Pi: ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--{safe_cwd}--/), so the home dir is granted writable+readable wholesale. No mechanism scopes reads to the current workspace's session subdir.

## Fix (dynamic, spawn-time; depends on cwd so not a static profile)
1. blanket deny_read on ~/.pi/agent/sessions (tmpfs mount).
2. rw-bind back ONLY the current workspace's `--{safe_cwd}--` subdir (Pi needs write).
   Mechanism already exists: strict re-binds ~/.config/oqto via extra_ro_bind AFTER the deny_read tmpfs (config.rs line ~561). Same layering.
3. Wire the unused `_workspace` param in spawn.rs to compute safe_cwd and inject the bind.
4. Generalize to ~/.claude and ~/.codex session/history dirs.

## Granularity
- Default: workspace-scoped (whole --safe_cwd-- subdir) -> maps to oqto-log Workspace scope.
- strict: session-file-only.

## Notes
- Found while building operator analytics CLI (~/scripts/bash/pi-sessions, trx oqto-qjcy). That tool is operator-only and intentionally NOT exposed to agents.
- Agent-facing session search is the correct path and already partly built (oqto-log FTS5 search_timeline); see epic oqto-2hyk.
- Add a regression test: agent in workspace A cannot read workspace B's session JSONL.

Implemented canonical session-ID persistence hardening for Pi JSONL imports to stop frontend history splits (messages present in JSONL but split across two oqto_log_sessions).

Root cause documented:
- duplicate oqto_log_sessions for same external_id (Pi session ID), e.g. one oqto-* platform session plus one legacy external-id session
- non-deterministic external_id lookup (`find_session_by_external ... LIMIT 1`) could pick the wrong row
- post-pass importer repair could write using mismatch session token directly, reintroducing split identity rows

Changes shipped:
1) backend/crates/oqto-history/src/oqto_log/ops.rs
   - `find_session_by_external` now deterministically picks canonical session:
     - prefer session_id==platform_id and `oqto-*`
     - then highest turn_count
     - then newest updated_at
   - added `list_sessions_by_external_in_workspace(...)`
   - added `delete_session_in_workspace(...)`

2) backend/crates/oqto/src/oqto_log/importer.rs
   - added `collapse_duplicate_external_sessions(...)` helper
   - after successful import/replace, collapse duplicate sessions for same external_id keeping canonical session only
   - fixed post-pass mismatch repair:
     - resolve mismatch token to canonical session/external IDs before replace
     - locate JSONL by resolved external ID
     - replace canonical session, then collapse duplicates

Validation:
- cargo fmt -p oqto -p oqto-history
- cargo check -p oqto-history -p oqto

Expected effect:
- no more split timelines where frontend shows only subset of messages while Pi JSONL has full history
- existing duplicates are automatically collapsed on subsequent import/repair passes

mmry: Append-Only Memory Architecture [lest-ills-trip]

changes.to:
## Goal

Migrate oqto from the legacy `mmry service run` / HTTP proxy integration to embedded `mmry-core` workspace-local memory files.

Target model:

```text
<workspace>/.mmry/mmry.jsonl
```

Use `mmry-core` directly from the oqto runner/user-plane. Do not depend on per-user mmry services, ports, TOML config, legacy stores, or `/v1/memories` proxying.

## mmry-core API

Use the renamed JSONL layer:

```rust
use mmry_core::{MemoryEntry, MemoryEvent, MemoryEventType, MemoryFile};
use mmry_core::agent_ctx::AgentCtx;
```

Open/init workspace memory:

```rust
let memory_file = MemoryFile::open_workspace(workspace_path);
memory_file.init(false)?;
```

Add memory:

```rust
let event = MemoryEvent::add(content, memory_type, tags, &AgentCtx::from_env());
memory_file.append(&event)?;
```

List memories:

```rust
let memories = memory_file.active_memories()?;
```

Search memories:

```rust
let hits = memory_file.search(query, limit)?;
```

Delete/remove memory:

```rust
let event = MemoryEvent::deprecate(memory_id, &AgentCtx::from_env());
memory_file.append(&event)?;
```

Deletion is append-only deprecation, not physical deletion.

## API mapping for existing frontend

Map `MemoryEntry` to the current frontend shape:

```text
id          <- memory_id
content     <- content
memory_type <- memory_type
tags        <- tags
created_at  <- created_at
updated_at  <- updated_at
metadata    <- metadata
category    <- metadata.category ?? "general"
importance  <- metadata.importance ?? 5
```

For update/edit, either:

```text
deprecate old memory + add replacement memory
```

or temporarily remove/disable edit support if simpler.

## Remove/replace oqto service integration

Replace dependencies on:

```text
mmry service run
~/.config/mmry/config.toml
per-user mmry ports
legacy stores
/v1/memories proxying
semantic/rerank memory service
```

Likely touched files:

```text
scripts/setup/18-services.sh
deploy/docker/entrypoint.sh
deploy/systemd/oqto-runner.service
deploy/systemd/mmry-embeddings.service
backend/crates/oqto/src/local/user_mmry.rs
backend/crates/oqto-host/src/linux_users.rs
backend/crates/oqto/src/api/proxy/mmry.rs
backend/crates/oqto/src/api/routes.rs
backend/crates/oqto/src/user_plane/*
```

Replace `/api/workspace/memories*` with direct user-plane/runner calls into `mmry-core`.

## Behavior changes

Intentional short-term behavior:

```text
local lexical search only
workspace-local memories only
append-only JSONL source of truth
```

No short-term compatibility path for:

```text
semantic search
reranking
named stores
global stores
session dumps
service config
```

## Migration of existing memories

Use the mmry migration script, filtering out bloated hstry/session imports by default:

```bash
scripts/migrate_legacy_mmry_to_jsonl.py ~/.local/share/mmry/stores/mmry.db \
  --store oqto \
  -o ../oqto_refactor/.mmry/mmry.jsonl
```

Better long-term: migrate legacy store buckets into their corresponding repo workspaces, e.g. `oqto` memories into oqto workspace, `octo` memories into octo workspace, etc.

## Notes

This intentionally makes `mmry` the distilled durable-memory substrate, not a second session search/index. Session search and semantic/human search should live in separate tools/layers.

changes.from:
Goal
Create one clear, auditable, low-drift deploy/update pipeline for Oqto by converging setup and deploy onto a single release layout and contract-driven activation flow.

Problem summary
- Two active deployment models exist today (transactional releases vs direct install/copy).
- Shipped vs editable files are not encoded in one authoritative manifest.
- Multi-user drift remains likely when files are copied ad hoc into user/system locations.
- Update behavior is split across setup update and deploy paths.

Outcome (definition of done)
1) One canonical runtime/install layout with explicit immutable/mutable layers.
2) One authoritative shipped-asset manifest in-repo, consumed by both setup and deploy.
3) Setup and deploy share a single activation/update mechanism.
4) Copy-vs-symlink policy enforced from manifest classes.
5) Workdir template and ~/.pi layering documented and implemented consistently.
6) Doctor/strict gates integrated pre/post activation.
7) Migration path for existing installs without downtime/data loss.

Scope
- Oqto repo deployment and setup architecture only.
- No behavioral changes to chat/session protocol beyond setup/deploy integration points.

Non-goals
- Rewriting all shell to Rust in one shot.
- Introducing a broad root daemon.

Acceptance evidence
- New docs + manifest committed.
- setup/deploy commands produce identical release activation semantics.
- E2E checks demonstrate no regressions for personal and team modes.

changes.from: Implement secure RPC secret submission path: client -> runner -> kyz (no agent transcript exposure)
changes.to: Secure secret submission: client -> runner -> SecretProvider (no agent transcript exposure)

changes.from:
Goal
Add a secure secret submission and use flow for RPC clients that routes secrets from client to owning runner and into runner-local kyz, without exposing secret values to agent/model transcripts, chat history, or tool logs.

Why
- Pi core cannot be changed; solution must be extension + Oqto platform.
- RPC clients need parity with TUI secure secret workflows.
- Future remote runners require locality: secret resolution/injection should happen on runner host.

Architecture
- Data path (secret bytes): Client -> Backend -> Runner -> kyz (local on runner host)
- Control path (metadata only): extension/agent commands and status events
- Secret values must never flow through chat message content, tool args shown to model, or persisted history.

Scope
1) Canonical RPC command additions (agent/files/ws channel as appropriate)
   - secret.submit (runner-routed)
   - secret.submit_status / command_response (metadata only)
   Payload (submit):
   - request_id (uuid)
   - session_id (platform session)
   - workspace_path (optional but preferred)
   - service, key
   - value (sensitive payload)
   - expires_at (short TTL)
   - origin metadata (client build/user id/device id)

2) Backend relay hardening
   - Route sensitive command only to owning runner of session/workspace.
   - Mark payload as sensitive in tracing pipeline:
     - no structured logs of value
     - no websocket debug echo of value
     - no persistence in hstry/oqto-log
   - Enforce max payload size and required fields.

3) Runner secure handling
   - Accept secret.submit only from authenticated backend channel.
   - Validate request_id TTL and replay window (request_id dedup cache).
   - Forward value to local kyz endpoint/CLI stdin path without shell interpolation.
   - Immediately zero/drop in-memory buffers post-use where practical.
   - Return success/failure + denial code (no value in error text).

4) Policy/authorization checks
   - Session/workspace ownership check (user cannot submit to foreign runner/session).
   - Optional allowlist for service/key namespaces per workspace/org policy.
   - Deny with explicit taxonomy: unauthorized, expired, replay, invalid_payload, out_of_scope, kyz_unavailable.

5) Audit events (non-sensitive)
   - Emit metadata-only audit records:
     - ts, user_id, session_id, runner_id, workspace, service/key, request_id, outcome, denial_code
   - Never include secret value or derived encodings.

6) Extension integration contract (pi-kyz)
   - RPC mode: /kyz-set must not solicit plaintext in chat.
   - Extension triggers secure client flow and awaits submit_status.
   - TUI mode can continue local masked input path.

7) Remote-runner readiness
   - Ensure backend always routes to runner-local kyz; no backend-global secret store fallback.
   - Define failure behavior when runner offline (queued? reject?). Prefer explicit reject with retry guidance.

Security requirements
- No value in logs (backend/runner/frontend), telemetry, traces, or persisted events.
- No value in command previews/tool output shown to LLM.
- No shell command interpolation containing secret value.
- Replay + expiry enforcement mandatory.
- Request correlation via request_id only.

Testing
A) Unit
- Payload redaction tests in backend logging path.
- Replay/expiry checks in runner.
- Ownership/authorization checks.

B) Integration
- End-to-end RPC submit success: secret appears in kyz on runner host.
- Verify no secret appears in:
  - browser console
  - backend logs
  - runner logs
  - hstry/oqto-log messages/events
- Denial-path tests: expired, replayed, unauthorized, malformed.

C) E2E (agent-browser)
- Trigger /kyz-set in RPC client flow.
- Complete secure form/input on client.
- Confirm agent receives only success message.
- Use secret via kyz exec/pipe path successfully.

Acceptance criteria
1. RPC client can set secret via client->runner->kyz with no transcript exposure.
2. Secret value is absent from all logs/history/events by automated checks.
3. Replay and expiry protections are enforced.
4. Ownership checks prevent cross-session/workspace misuse.
5. Works with remote runner topology (runner-local kyz only).

Out of scope
- Pi core changes.
- Full centralized secret broker replacing kyz.
- Bulk secret replication to runner hosts.
changes.to: Per ADR-0007. Path is client -> runner -> SecretProvider, where SecretProvider is pluggable (kyz/Infisical/Vault/env), not kyz-hardcoded. Secrets never enter the agent transcript or env in cleartext.

changes.from: NetworkMode::Proxy is config-only today; live posture is binary Open (full network) or Isolated (--unshare-net). Implement real egress capture for sandboxed agents: (1) confine agent in its own network namespace with a single host-managed veth; (2) host-side nftables DNAT all TCP to a transparent proxy (eavs in TPROXY/forward mode), force DNS to a controlled resolver, default-DROP all other traffic (UDP incl QUIC, ICMP, raw); (3) seccomp deny AF_PACKET/SOCK_RAW, no CAP_NET_ADMIN for agent. This is the enforcement half without which any credential-injection layer is bypassable via plain curl to arbitrary hosts. Note limits honestly: holds against misbehaving clients and in-sandbox processes, NOT against kernel LPE (that is the microvm tier). Design context: docs/active/design/20260609-isolation-tiers-and-egress.md
changes.to: Per ADR-0007. The egress PROXY already exists in eavs (eavs/src/egress.rs: transparent firewall, PROXY v2, SNI/Host domain ACL, DNS relay). The REMAINING work is the sandbox-side netns + DNAT redirect FRONT-END that captures agent traffic and feeds eavs over PROXY v2. Do not build a second proxy. changes.from:
ROOT CAUSE: under userns-enabled profiles, bwrap (--unshare-user) writes into the host-shared workspace target/ under an unmapped in-ns uid -> files land as 'nobody' (overflow uid 65534) on the host, which the workspace owner cannot overwrite. Breaks subsequent host AND agent builds; recurs every sandboxed build.

WHY OVERLAY (not uid-map fix): COW overlay read-shares the host build cache (fast first build) while writes go to a private upper layer (zero host pollution) AND is safe under concurrency (two builders in one target/ race on fingerprints/locks even with correct uids). Overlay is already IMPLEMENTED (oqto-sandbox/src/config.rs ~1714-1774: per-workspace upper/work dirs, bwrap --overlay-src/--overlay), gated by overlay_enabled.

THE GAP: overlay_paths currently covers only package caches (~/.cargo, ~/.npm, ~/.bun, ~/.local/share/uv, ~/.cache/uv), NOT the workspace target/. target/ lives inside the rw workspace bind (source must persist). So enabling overlay alone does NOT fix this.

FIX: extend overlay coverage to build-output dirs (rust target/, node build artifacts) as a subdir overlay on top of the rw workspace, so source round-trips rw while build output is COW-isolated. Then enable in default profiles. Consequence: agent build output becomes ephemeral (per-session upper layer) - acceptable; deliverable artifacts go through explicit output paths. Add GC for ~/.oqto/overlays upper dirs. Needs a repro + real sandbox testing (cannot build/verify in the Claude Code harness). Related: oqto-b4za (closed, uid_map/Landlock ordering).
changes.to:
Sandboxed agent builds write nobody-owned files into the shared host target/, breaking subsequent host AND agent builds. Recurs every sandboxed build.

== CURRENT BEHAVIOR (verified from code, oqto-sandbox/src/config.rs + oqto-runner/src/pi_manager.rs + spawn.rs) ==
1. Cache + build dirs are raw rw bind-throughs to the REAL host paths: ~/.cargo etc. are in allow_write -> rw --bind; workspace is '--bind workspace workspace' (config.rs:1601) and target/ lives inside it. overlay_enabled=false in ALL profiles (555/622/688). No overlay, no redirect -> agent build and host build write the SAME physical files.
2. bwrap gets NO explicit uid map: grep for setuid/seteuid/--uid/--gid/runuser in the bwrap spawn path is EMPTY. --unshare-user is emitted only when disable_userns=true (development, strict; config.rs:1880-1883); minimal gets no userns. With --unshare-user and no --uid, bwrap uses its default single-entry map (spawning euid -> same uid in-ns); every other in-ns uid resolves to the host overflow uid = nobody (65534).
3. So ownership of writes is unmanaged: writes under the one mapped uid are owned correctly; writes under any other in-ns uid land as nobody. Runner can operate euid 0 (egress.rs:334) and there is NO drop to the workspace owner before the build, so the map covers one identity while writes occur under another -> nobody on host.
LIMIT: exact uid attribution (why nobody vs runner-user) needs a live 'cat /proc/<build-pid>/uid_map' during repro; the three facts above are code-verified. Net: today there is NEITHER isolation NOR uid management on cache/build writes.

== WHY OVERLAY (not chmod, not uid-only) ==
COW overlay read-shares the host cache (fast) while writes go to a private upper layer (zero host pollution) AND is concurrency-safe (two builders in one target/ race on fingerprints/locks even with correct uids). 'chmod-wide' fails: doesn't fix ownership (userns, not mode), doesn't fix concurrency, and opens a cache-poisoning / cross-tenant write channel (agents write each other's/your ~/.cargo). Overlay is already IMPLEMENTED (config.rs ~1714-1774: per-workspace upper/work, bwrap --overlay-src/--overlay), gated by overlay_enabled.

== THE GAP ==
overlay_paths covers only package caches (~/.cargo,~/.npm,~/.bun,~/.local/share/uv,~/.cache/uv), NOT the workspace target/ (which lives in the rw workspace bind). Enabling overlay alone does NOT fix this.

== FIX ==
Extend overlay coverage to build-output dirs (rust target/, node build artifacts) as a subdir overlay ON TOP OF the rw workspace, so source round-trips rw while build output is COW-isolated; enable in profiles. Consequence: agent build output ephemeral (per-session upper) - acceptable; deliverables go via explicit output paths. Add GC for ~/.oqto/overlays upper dirs. Needs repro + real sandbox testing (cannot build in Claude Code harness).
SINGLE-USER ALTERNATIVE: for personal/non-concurrent boxes, fixing the bwrap uid map so writes round-trip to the workspace owner gives a shared+persistent+correctly-owned cache without overlay's ephemerality. Pick per-profile: uid-map for personal, overlay for team/multi-user. Related: oqto-b4za (closed, uid_map/Landlock ordering).

changes.to:
Sandboxed agent builds write nobody-owned files into the shared host target/, breaking subsequent host AND agent builds. Recurs every sandboxed build.

== CURRENT BEHAVIOR (verified from code, oqto-sandbox/src/config.rs + oqto-runner/src/pi_manager.rs + spawn.rs) ==
1. Cache + build dirs are raw rw bind-throughs to the REAL host paths: ~/.cargo etc. are in allow_write -> rw --bind; workspace is '--bind workspace workspace' (config.rs:1601) and target/ lives inside it. overlay_enabled=false in ALL profiles (555/622/688). No overlay, no redirect -> agent build and host build write the SAME physical files.
2. bwrap gets NO explicit uid map: grep for setuid/seteuid/--uid/--gid/runuser in the bwrap spawn path is EMPTY. --unshare-user is emitted only when disable_userns=true (development, strict; config.rs:1880-1883); minimal gets no userns. With --unshare-user and no --uid, bwrap uses its default single-entry map (spawning euid -> same uid in-ns); every other in-ns uid resolves to the host overflow uid = nobody (65534).
3. So ownership of writes is unmanaged: writes under the one mapped uid are owned correctly; writes under any other in-ns uid land as nobody. Runner can operate euid 0 (egress.rs:334) and there is NO drop to the workspace owner before the build, so the map covers one identity while writes occur under another -> nobody on host.
LIMIT: exact uid attribution (why nobody vs runner-user) needs a live 'cat /proc/<build-pid>/uid_map' during repro; the three facts above are code-verified. Net: today there is NEITHER isolation NOR uid management on cache/build writes.

== WHY OVERLAY (not chmod, not uid-only) ==
COW overlay read-shares the host cache (fast) while writes go to a private upper layer (zero host pollution) AND is concurrency-safe (two builders in one target/ race on fingerprints/locks even with correct uids). 'chmod-wide' fails: doesn't fix ownership (userns, not mode), doesn't fix concurrency, and opens a cache-poisoning / cross-tenant write channel (agents write each other's/your ~/.cargo). Overlay is already IMPLEMENTED (config.rs ~1714-1774: per-workspace upper/work, bwrap --overlay-src/--overlay), gated by overlay_enabled.

== THE GAP ==
overlay_paths covers only package caches (~/.cargo,~/.npm,~/.bun,~/.local/share/uv,~/.cache/uv), NOT the workspace target/ (which lives in the rw workspace bind). Enabling overlay alone does NOT fix this.

== FIX ==
Extend overlay coverage to build-output dirs (rust target/, node build artifacts) as a subdir overlay ON TOP OF the rw workspace, so source round-trips rw while build output is COW-isolated; enable in profiles. Consequence: agent build output ephemeral (per-session upper) - acceptable; deliverables go via explicit output paths. Add GC for ~/.oqto/overlays upper dirs. Needs repro + real sandbox testing (cannot build in Claude Code harness).
SINGLE-USER ALTERNATIVE: for personal/non-concurrent boxes, fixing the bwrap uid map so writes round-trip to the workspace owner gives a shared+persistent+correctly-owned cache without overlay's ephemerality. Pick per-profile: uid-map for personal, overlay for team/multi-user. Related: oqto-b4za (closed, uid_map/Landlock ordering).

== PERFORMANCE PROFILE (overlay) ==
RAM: flat/negligible. bwrap --overlay is kernel overlayfs; upper/work live on overlay_root=~/.oqto/overlays (config.rs:135), regular DISK not tmpfs -> no RAM-backed storage. Only cost is small kernel inode/dentry metadata for the merged view. Lower-layer reads share the host page cache (no double-caching). RULE: never put overlay_root on tmpfs or RAM cost becomes real.
CPU: small, usually unnoticeable. (a) thin per-path lookup (check upper then lower) - single-digit % at worst on metadata-heavy build workloads; (b) copy-up only when MODIFYING a file that exists in the lower layer - mostly N/A here since ~/.cargo is read-mostly and new build artifacts are created directly in upper (no copy-up).
DISK: the real cost. Each session's upper layer accumulates that session's build output (a Rust target/ is GBs); one overlay per sandbox session. ~/.oqto/overlays grows fast without GC. Concurrent builds multiply DISK, not RAM. Size GC + disk budget accordingly (this is what the GC requirement above is for).

changes.to:
Make "each personal user or shared workspace runs as its own container with a runner inside it" a first-class Placement (NOT a backend runtime mode — ADR-0001). Decision records: docs/adr/0019-container-per-workspace-placement.md + docs/adr/0020-portability-oci-substrate-pluggable-supervisor.md.

Resolved design (grilled 2026-06-25):
- Workspace = Principal = container; Workspace = a Pod (runner container + shared infra wired as endpoints). 1 runner per Workspace. Personal default: 1 container per Account; shared: always its own container.
- Generalizes the existing shared-workspace seam (workspace_id -> dedicated Principal -> runner socket) to (Workspace -> container -> in-container runner via bind-mounted unix socket). Backend routing barely changes; placement invisible to protocol.
- Portability (ADR-0020): OCI substrate; pluggable Placement Supervisor; rootless podman PRIMARY on every OS (podman machine on Mac/Win); k8s + Docker + local-process as backends; systemd demoted to one backend.
- Drop host Linux users: isolation via container + per-Workspace userns subuid ranges; oqto-hostd shrinks to subuid-alloc + container start.
- Data: filesystem-as-truth, shared-nothing; per-Workspace volume holds oqto-log SQLite + mmry + files, single-writer-local; container = ephemeral compute, volume = durable truth.
- eavs: shared node/cluster service by default, wired as an egress endpoint; runner topology-agnostic; per-Workspace sidecar is opt-in only.
- Sandbox under in-container (reduced-cap) root: runner applies Landlock+seccomp before exec with NO_NEW_PRIVS (irrevocable even by root); no CAP_SYS_ADMIN; cross-tenant (userns) and intra-Workspace (landlock) are independent layers; capability advertisement + graceful degradation where Landlock absent.
- Operability is a first-class deliverable (labels + oqtoctl debug verbs + registry); transparency relocates host -> control plane.

Blocked on: oqto-3ct7.16 (PlacementStore contract), oqto-3ct7.15 (delete dead container/RuntimeMode code).
Downstream of: ADR-0018 / oqto-vemr.9 (complete prebuilt bundle feeds the per-Workspace image).

Open: remote reachability (dial-in), mount-source future types, resource governance.

changes.to:
Enforcement half of ADR-0021. Implemented as ordered sub-steps; CROSS-REPO (byteowlz/byt + byteowlz/.github). Decisions: docs/adr/0021 (spec) + docs/adr/0022 (byt distribution).

Sub-steps (in order):
1. Decide+bootstrap byt distribution (ADR-0022): build container image ghcr.io/byteowlz/byt bundling byt + cargo-zigbuild/zig + rust + go, from source ONCE (one-off byt-repo workflow or local docker build), push to GHCR (private; pulled from same-org Actions via GITHUB_TOKEN). byt is private with 0 releases today, so this is the unlock.
   Interim option to prove the flow before the image exists: cargo install --git (with token) on a rust runner.
2. Implement the `byt release` subcommand per ADR-0021:
   - subcommands: build [--target T] / checksums / publish [--tag] / verify <dir|url> / all-in-one; --dry-run everywhere.
   - per-repo byt.release.toml: name, bins[], targets[], extra[], sign, lang.
   - delegate ONLY compile to language backends (cargo-zigbuild for Rust, go for Go); byt owns staging (top-level {name}-v{ver}-{triple}/ dir with bin/ + LICENSE/README), tar.gz naming, checksums.txt, optional signing, gh release publish.
   - after first image, byt self-hosts its own releases.
3. Reusable workflow byteowlz/.github/.github/workflows/release.yml: job runs `container: ghcr.io/byteowlz/byt:vN`, checkout, `byt release` (GITHUB_TOKEN). Consumer repos call it pinned to a tag (~3-line release.yml).

Caveat: container: jobs are Linux-only -> covers required linux x86_64/aarch64 (zigbuild). Native darwin/windows need a prebuilt byt binary via a byteowlz/setup-byt action; defer until wanted.

Done when: a tag push on a conforming repo produces spec-shaped artifacts (oqto-setup acquire verifies them end-to-end).

changes.from:
Make byteowlz tools truly cross-platform (audit 2026-06-28). Cross-repo; tracked from the oqto tracker.

CANONICAL CONFIG-DIR RULE (option B, decided): an explicit XDG_* env var wins on EVERY OS; otherwise ~/.config-style on all unix INCLUDING macOS (deliberately NOT ~/Library/Application Support for CLI tools), and native APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA on Windows.

  config:  $XDG_CONFIG_HOME | ~/.config        (unix incl mac) | %APPDATA%      (win)
  data:    $XDG_DATA_HOME   | ~/.local/share   (unix incl mac) | %APPDATA%      (win)
  state:   $XDG_STATE_HOME  | ~/.local/state   (unix incl mac) | %LOCALAPPDATA% (win)
  cache:   $XDG_CACHE_HOME  | ~/.cache         (unix incl mac) | %LOCALAPPDATA% (win)

Delivery: a small vendored paths helper (~20 lines, uses the dirs crate only for the Windows defaults; never dirs::config_dir on mac, which would give ~/Library). Vendored per-repo (consistent with ADR-0017 vendor-not-publish), NOT a shared published crate.

Audit verdicts: truly cross-platform already = agntz, ignr, skdlr, tmpltr, scrpr. Needs work = mmry (hard Windows compile blocker), eavs, trx, sx, byt, sldr (cosmetic). macOS already works for ALL tools; Windows is the only real frontier.

changes.from:
"Get binary X onto a host" exists as 4 divergent implementations (ADR-0018). Collapse to ONE manifest-driven path that downloads prebuilt, checksummed artifacts.

## The 4 to collapse
1. scripts/install.sh — download release tarball + oqto-setup install (the good path / keep as bootstrap)
2. deploy/docker/Dockerfile downloader stage — downloads every binary from GitHub releases (reference behavior)
3. scripts/setup/08-agent-tools.sh `download_or_build_tool` — release download + cargo-install fallback (DELETE)
4. scripts/deploy.sh `remediate_dependency()` — release download + cargo-install-from-source fallback (DELETE)

## Plan
- One acquisition function in the typed core, driven by dist/manifest.toml + dependencies.toml pins.
- release.yml publishes a COMPLETE prebuilt bundle: oqto's crates AND byteowlz deps (trx, mmry, eavs, agntz, mailz, sx, scrpr, tmpltr, sldr, skdlr, ignr). Currently release.yml only ships oqto's own binaries.
- `just install-deps` / `install-all` stop building ~12 sibling repos from source by default; build-from-source moves behind an explicit dev flag (ADR-0018).
- Verify checksums on every download; fail closed on mismatch.

## Done when
- Exactly one code path downloads/installs component binaries; 08-agent-tools.sh and remediate_dependency() deleted.
- A fresh host installs the full stack from the published bundle with no Rust/cargo toolchain present.

## References
docs/adr/0018-single-install-update-deploy-engine.md

- `oqto-setup acquire --install-bin <dir>` exposes it; `just acquire-deps` is the additive prebuilt install path. Verified E2E against live releases (oqto bin/ layout + mmry flat multi-binary). dependencies.toml refreshed to current versions.

changes.from:
DISCOVERED on a clean Ubuntu 22.04 box (ubuntu-builder, glibc 2.35), 2026-06-30:
the freshly-released *-unknown-linux-gnu artifacts download + checksum-verify but FAIL TO RUN:
  trx v0.6.2  -> GLIBC_2.39 not found
  eavs v0.7.1 -> GLIBC_2.39 not found
  ignr 0.1.2  -> runs OK (doesn't hit a 2.39 symbol / older runner)
Cause: GitHub `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` is now 24.04 (glibc 2.39); dynamically-linked gnu binaries built there require glibc >= 2.39 and won't run on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (glibc 2.35) or older — a common deploy target. This breaks vemr.9's prebuilt-install promise (oqto-setup acquire --install-bin installs binaries that can't run).

FIX (release build side): build linux releases against a glibc FLOOR so they run on old + new:
  - Preferred: cargo-zigbuild --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.28 (zig sets the glibc floor; the byt builder image already has cargo-zigbuild — ADR-0022). Pick a floor (2.28 = RHEL8/Ubuntu 18.04+, or 2.31 = Ubuntu 20.04+).
  - Alternative: ship x86_64-unknown-linux-musl static binaries (run anywhere; some C-dep caveats e.g. openssl -> vendored).
Bake the glibc floor into the byt release spec (ADR-0021) so every repo's artifacts are portable. Then REBUILD the affected releases (trx, eavs, and any other Rust tool built on 24.04).

Also: add a clean-old-glibc smoke test to the release/acquire E2E (run --version on Ubuntu 22.04) so this regresses loudly.

changes.from: Canonize session-identity discipline as an ADR per govnr follow-up: single public Oqto session id across frontend/CLI/APIs/govnr; harness-native ids (pi JSONL, claude, codex thread, tmux pane, pid) are adapter-local bindings only; events after binding carry oqto_session_id; append-only auditable mappings; no pending-*/tmp:* across persistence/API boundaries; attach targets are capabilities not identity.
changes.to: BLOCKED: session lacked file-write permission to docs/adr; full ADR draft ready, needs to be written as docs/adr/0023-one-public-oqto-session-id-harness-ids-adapter-local.md. Decision (6 points): (1) One public id: the Oqto session id (= AGENT_CTX PLATFORM_SESSION_ID) is the only session identity on public surfaces (frontend routes, CLI/oqtoctl, REST/WS APIs, oqto-log keys, gvnr/govnr records, human refs); minted once by backend session authority, never re-minted across resume/reconnect/harness restart; forks get own id + parent_id lineage. (2) Harness/runtime ids (pi JSONL uuid, claude session id, codex thread id, ACP handle, tmux pane, pid) are adapter-local bindings owned by the translator that produced them; may travel as external_id facts, never primary key/route param/cross-component ref. (3) After binding, every event/persisted record carries oqto_session_id; external ids are optional annotations, never the join key. (4) oqto_session_id->external-id mappings are append-only auditable facts with provenance; rebinding appends, never updates in place. (5) pending-*/tmp:* ids never cross persistence/API boundaries; fail closed waiting for real id. (6) Attach targets (tmux/PTY/pid) are capabilities a session HAS (ADR-0006 capability set), not identity; attach addresses the Oqto session id. Fit: ADR-0003/0013 (PLATFORM_SESSION_ID join keys), ADR-0006 (capability advertisement), oqto_log_sessions.platform_id+external_id is reference schema. Consequences: frontend never mints identity; bridged adapters use the one mapping record; reconciliation-by-text/index/order stays banned; lint/doctor checks for pending-/tmp: leakage. NOTE: takes number 0023, so oqto-964n's planned ADR becomes 0024.

## Goal

Prove whether Herdr can serve as Oqto's first broad **observed session backend** for Claude Code, Codex TUI, OpenCode, Hermes, and other terminal harnesses, while preserving native Pi as the high-fidelity path.

This spike should reduce uncertainty, not build the final product. The expected output is a tested prototype plus a short decision note: adopt Herdr backend, reject it, or adopt with constraints.

## Context

Oqto's current strongest path is native Pi integration. That should remain. The missing capability is broad, low-friction orchestration and UI attach for other CLI/TUI harnesses without writing custom drivers for each one.

Herdr is installed locally and exposes a useful API surface:

- `herdr agent start <name> --cwd PATH --env KEY=VALUE -- <argv...>`
- `herdr agent list`
- `herdr agent get <target>`
- `herdr agent read <target> --lines N --format text|ansi`
- `herdr agent send <target> <text>`
- `herdr agent wait <target> --status idle|working|blocked|unknown`
- `herdr agent attach <target>`
- `herdr pane report-agent ...`

Herdr also has harness integrations for pi, Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, Cursor, Droid, etc. These can report semantic state, but Herdr ids must remain external bindings, never Oqto identity.

Relevant Oqto decisions:

- ADR-0001: runner is the sole execution interface.
- ADR-0006: Pi native first-class, other harnesses bridged/adapter-based.
- ADR-0013: host activity and `AGENT_CTX_*` injection.
- ADR-0019/0020: placement supervisor owns containers; runner is placement-blind and runs inside placement.
- ADR-0023: one public Oqto session id; harness ids are adapter-local bindings.

## Proposed model to test

```text
oqto-frontend / oqto-cli / govnr
        -> oqto-backend
        -> oqto-runner
        -> Herdr observed backend adapter
        -> claude | codex | opencode | hermes | pi fallback
```

Herdr provides terminal/session operations. Oqto still owns:

- `oqto_session_id`
- task / issue / repo metadata
- auth and backend tenancy
- oqto-log durable history authority
- Work Session read model
- placement and sandbox policy

Herdr facts are bindings/capabilities:

- `herdr_terminal_id`
- `herdr_pane_id`
- `herdr_workspace_id`
- `herdr_tab_id`
- `herdr_agent_label`

## Scope

Build a minimal prototype path, preferably in a small isolated module or spike branch, that can:

1. Start an observed Herdr-backed session from Oqto runner code or a temporary spike binary/script.
2. Inject required `AGENT_CTX_*`, especially:
   - `AGENT_CTX_PLATFORM_NAME=oqto`
   - `AGENT_CTX_PLATFORM_SESSION_ID=<oqto_session_id>`
   - `AGENT_CTX_WORKSPACE_PATH=<canonical host workspace>`
   - `AGENT_CTX_HARNESS=<claude|codex|opencode|...>`
   - `AGENT_CTX_TASK=<human task>`
   - `AGENT_CTX_ISSUE=<trx id if present>`
3. Record Herdr ids as external bindings/capabilities, not primary ids.
4. List active Herdr-backed observed sessions.
5. Read bounded terminal output.
6. Send text/input.
7. Surface Herdr status (`idle|working|blocked|unknown`) into an Oqto Work Session read-model draft.
8. Demonstrate attach path, even if only by returning an attach descriptor/command.
9. Show how this would be exposed to frontend/CLI/govnr without frontend knowing Herdr internals.

## Non-goals

- Do not replace native Pi integration.
- Do not make Herdr the source of Oqto session identity.
- Do not move container lifecycle into oqto-runner; placement supervisor remains owner.
- Do not build a full harness abstraction for every tool.
- Do not persist Herdr ids as API route ids.
- Do not implement final UI polish.

## Experiments / questions to answer

- Are Herdr ids stable enough for attach/read/send while treating them as external bindings?
- Can Herdr status integrations reliably distinguish idle/working/blocked for Claude, Codex, and OpenCode?
- Can Oqto inject `AGENT_CTX_*` through Herdr launch consistently?
- Can Herdr be used inside Oqto container placement, or does it need to run on the host/placement boundary?
- Does Herdr conflict with Oqto's sandbox model, or can it be an adapter inside the runner process environment?
- Can frontend terminal streaming be implemented from `herdr agent read` polling initially, or is a push/socket path required?
- What is the minimum attach contract Oqto needs for Herdr sessions?

## Deliverables

1. Spike code or script demonstrating Herdr-backed observed launch/read/send/status.
2. A short markdown note under `docs/spikes/` or `repo-analysis/` with:
   - commands run
   - what worked
   - what failed
   - fidelity tier recommendation
   - integration risks
   - next implementation issue(s)
3. If the spike succeeds, draft/update an ADR for:
   - Work Session read model
   - fidelity tiers (`native`, `bridged`, `observed`)
   - attach contract
   - Herdr as one observed backend adapter
4. Tests where practical, at least fake-command parsing tests for the adapter boundary if production code is touched.

## Proof of positive outcome

A reviewer should be able to run one documented command and see an Oqto-owned session that:

- has a stable Oqto session id;
- launches through Herdr;
- receives `AGENT_CTX_*`;
- appears in a Work Session-like listing with task, repo, harness, status, and attach info;
- supports read/send/attach using Oqto-facing commands or the spike script;
- never exposes Herdr ids as public session identity.

## Suggested first test command

Start with a harmless shell harness before using Claude/Codex:

```bash
herdr agent start oqto-spike --cwd /tmp \
  --env AGENT_CTX_PLATFORM_NAME=oqto \
  --env AGENT_CTX_PLATFORM_SESSION_ID=sess_spike_001 \
  --env AGENT_CTX_TASK="Herdr observed backend spike" \
  -- bash -lc 'echo READY; env | grep AGENT_CTX_ | sort; while IFS= read -r line; do echo GOT:$line; done'
```

Then test list/read/send/status. After that, test one real harness with minimal risk.

changes.from:
## Goal

Prove whether Herdr can serve as Oqto's first broad **observed session backend** for Claude Code, Codex TUI, OpenCode, Hermes, and other terminal harnesses, while preserving native Pi as the high-fidelity path.

This spike should reduce uncertainty, not build the final product. The expected output is a tested prototype plus a short decision note: adopt Herdr backend, reject it, or adopt with constraints.

## Context

Oqto's current strongest path is native Pi integration. That should remain. The missing capability is broad, low-friction orchestration and UI attach for other CLI/TUI harnesses without writing custom drivers for each one.

Herdr is installed locally and exposes a useful API surface:

- `herdr agent start <name> --cwd PATH --env KEY=VALUE -- <argv...>`
- `herdr agent list`
- `herdr agent get <target>`
- `herdr agent read <target> --lines N --format text|ansi`
- `herdr agent send <target> <text>`
- `herdr agent wait <target> --status idle|working|blocked|unknown`
- `herdr agent attach <target>`
- `herdr pane report-agent ...`

Herdr also has harness integrations for pi, Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, Cursor, Droid, etc. These can report semantic state, but Herdr ids must remain external bindings, never Oqto identity.

Relevant Oqto decisions:

- ADR-0001: runner is the sole execution interface.
- ADR-0006: Pi native first-class, other harnesses bridged/adapter-based.
- ADR-0013: host activity and `AGENT_CTX_*` injection.
- ADR-0019/0020: placement supervisor owns containers; runner is placement-blind and runs inside placement.
- ADR-0023: one public Oqto session id; harness ids are adapter-local bindings.

## Proposed model to test

```text
oqto-frontend / oqto-cli / govnr
        -> oqto-backend
        -> oqto-runner
        -> Herdr observed backend adapter
        -> claude | codex | opencode | hermes | pi fallback
```

Herdr provides terminal/session operations. Oqto still owns:

- `oqto_session_id`
- task / issue / repo metadata
- auth and backend tenancy
- oqto-log durable history authority
- Work Session read model
- placement and sandbox policy

Herdr facts are bindings/capabilities:

- `herdr_terminal_id`
- `herdr_pane_id`
- `herdr_workspace_id`
- `herdr_tab_id`
- `herdr_agent_label`

## Scope

Build a minimal prototype path, preferably in a small isolated module or spike branch, that can:

1. Start an observed Herdr-backed session from Oqto runner code or a temporary spike binary/script.
2. Inject required `AGENT_CTX_*`, especially:
   - `AGENT_CTX_PLATFORM_NAME=oqto`
   - `AGENT_CTX_PLATFORM_SESSION_ID=<oqto_session_id>`
   - `AGENT_CTX_WORKSPACE_PATH=<canonical host workspace>`
   - `AGENT_CTX_HARNESS=<claude|codex|opencode|...>`
   - `AGENT_CTX_TASK=<human task>`
   - `AGENT_CTX_ISSUE=<trx id if present>`
3. Record Herdr ids as external bindings/capabilities, not primary ids.
4. List active Herdr-backed observed sessions.
5. Read bounded terminal output.
6. Send text/input.
7. Surface Herdr status (`idle|working|blocked|unknown`) into an Oqto Work Session read-model draft.
8. Demonstrate attach path, even if only by returning an attach descriptor/command.
9. Show how this would be exposed to frontend/CLI/govnr without frontend knowing Herdr internals.

## Non-goals

- Do not replace native Pi integration.
- Do not make Herdr the source of Oqto session identity.
- Do not move container lifecycle into oqto-runner; placement supervisor remains owner.
- Do not build a full harness abstraction for every tool.
- Do not persist Herdr ids as API route ids.
- Do not implement final UI polish.

## Experiments / questions to answer

- Are Herdr ids stable enough for attach/read/send while treating them as external bindings?
- Can Herdr status integrations reliably distinguish idle/working/blocked for Claude, Codex, and OpenCode?
- Can Oqto inject `AGENT_CTX_*` through Herdr launch consistently?
- Can Herdr be used inside Oqto container placement, or does it need to run on the host/placement boundary?
- Does Herdr conflict with Oqto's sandbox model, or can it be an adapter inside the runner process environment?
- Can frontend terminal streaming be implemented from `herdr agent read` polling initially, or is a push/socket path required?
- What is the minimum attach contract Oqto needs for Herdr sessions?

## Deliverables

1. Spike code or script demonstrating Herdr-backed observed launch/read/send/status.
2. A short markdown note under `docs/spikes/` or `repo-analysis/` with:
   - commands run
   - what worked
   - what failed
   - fidelity tier recommendation
   - integration risks
   - next implementation issue(s)
3. If the spike succeeds, draft/update an ADR for:
   - Work Session read model
   - fidelity tiers (`native`, `bridged`, `observed`)
   - attach contract
   - Herdr as one observed backend adapter
4. Tests where practical, at least fake-command parsing tests for the adapter boundary if production code is touched.

## Proof of positive outcome

A reviewer should be able to run one documented command and see an Oqto-owned session that:

- has a stable Oqto session id;
- launches through Herdr;
- receives `AGENT_CTX_*`;
- appears in a Work Session-like listing with task, repo, harness, status, and attach info;
- supports read/send/attach using Oqto-facing commands or the spike script;
- never exposes Herdr ids as public session identity.

## Suggested first test command

Start with a harmless shell harness before using Claude/Codex:

```bash
herdr agent start oqto-spike --cwd /tmp \
  --env AGENT_CTX_PLATFORM_NAME=oqto \
  --env AGENT_CTX_PLATFORM_SESSION_ID=sess_spike_001 \
  --env AGENT_CTX_TASK="Herdr observed backend spike" \
  -- bash -lc 'echo READY; env | grep AGENT_CTX_ | sort; while IFS= read -r line; do echo GOT:$line; done'
```

Then test list/read/send/status. After that, test one real harness with minimal risk.

Symptom: a session started via one client shows incomplete/divergent chat history when reopened from another machine.

Root cause (evidence, workspace store oqto-log/45661ed61681d8d746e393d4): one pi session (pi UUID 019f5f22-3777-78b7-ab0e-539863fb8232) produced TWO oqto_log_sessions rows for the same conversation:
  1. session_id=platform_id=external_id=019f5f22..., source_kind=pi_agent_end (live streaming path), 12 turns
  2. session_id=platform_id=oqto-1784007500905-e4b1aea20b3398, external_id=019f5f22..., source_kind=pi_jsonl (import path), 13 turns

Live path (oqto-runner/src/pi_manager.rs ~3742) calls append_agent_end_snapshot with session_id AND platform_id both == the raw pi UUID, because pi_manager.rs:3260 `pi_native_id_known = !session_id.starts_with("oqto-")` treats any non-oqto session_id as the pi-native id and never uses a canonical oqto public id. JSONL import path mints oqto-.... Two ingestion paths => two sessions for one conversation => history splits across reload/machines.

Violates ADR-0023 (one public oqto session id; platform_id=Oqto identity, external_id=harness binding; harness ids never become public/join ids) and the sacred session-identity rule.

Fix scope: (1) runner always operates under a minted oqto- id, pi UUID only as external_id, remove starts_with(oqto-) heuristic, fail-closed; (2) trace the start/attach entrypoint that admits a non-oqto session_id; (3) one-time reconciliation of duplicated rows; (4) regression test (one pi session => exactly one oqto_log_session across live+jsonl).

Related: ADR-0023, oqto-zpvs.5, oqto-964n.

## Summary
Live chat rendering is regressing across several related surfaces:
- each streaming text delta can be applied twice immediately, corrupting Markdown
- tool calls and results can split into orphan rows
- some tool spinners never reach a terminal state
- an active logical session can appear twice in the sidebar
- switching chats misses the <50 ms cached-first-paint target

Screenshots: uploads/IMG_8966.jpeg and uploads/IMG_8967.png.

## Required diagnostic
Build a deterministic trace/replay that records cardinality at Pi raw, runner translated, backend WS sent, frontend WS received, and reducer applied boundaries. Correlate by oqto_session_id, turn_id, message_id, part/tool_call_id, sequence/event id, connection id, and subscription id. Identify the first boundary where one event becomes two; do not deduplicate by text/index/order.

## Architecture constraints
- oqto-log is durable timeline authority; stream events are transient overlays.
- One backend-minted Oqto session id is public; harness ids remain adapter-local.
- No pending/tmp ids in persistence or public APIs.
- Tool call/result pairing uses canonical identity, never adjacency.
- Reload/reconnect must converge to the same canonical timeline.

## Acceptance proof
- deterministic test reproduces immediate duplicate deltas before fix and passes after
- one stream event is applied at most once through the frontend path
- partial and final Markdown render correctly
- tool result remains paired and every tool reaches success/error/abort terminal UI state
- no duplicate durable/sidebar session for create/stream/rename/reconnect
- measured cached chat-switch first paint is <50 ms at p95 in the test fixture
- relevant frontend/backend format, lint, test, generated-type, and E2E gates pass

## Evidence required
Attach trace cardinality, changed files, exact test commands/results, reload/reconnect parity, and any remaining environmental gaps.

## Summary
Live chat rendering regressed across related surfaces:
- immediate duplicate streaming deltas corrupt Markdown
- tool calls/results can split and spinners can remain active
- active logical session can appear twice in sidebar
- chat switching misses <50 ms target

Screenshots: uploads/IMG_8966.jpeg and uploads/IMG_8967.png.

## Diagnosis 2026-07-14
Immediate adjacent token duplication proves additive stream.text_delta is applied twice before Markdown rendering. Frontend ws-manager allowed a Set of multiple session handlers and fanned each event to all of them; useChat creates replacement closures while reattaching/resubscribing. Existing diagnostics explicitly warned that this state causes duplicate processing, but did not prevent it. Backend session.create has a per-connection pi_subscriptions guard, making the frontend fan-out the most defensible first duplication boundary. Runtime boundary trace could not be captured from this host/browser session.

## Fix in workspace
- frontend/lib/ws-manager.ts now enforces one timeline owner per session; a new subscription atomically replaces the old handler.
- stale unsubscribe closures remove only themselves and cannot remove the replacement owner.
- frontend/tests/ws-manager-session-owner.test.ts covers single delivery and stale-unsubscribe safety.

## Evidence
PASS: bun run test:run -- tests/ws-manager-session-owner.test.ts (2/2).
PASS: tool-output-leak (6/6), tool-summaries (10/10).
PASS: Biome and oxlint on touched files.
KNOWN PRE-EXISTING/UNRELATED FAILURE: trace-replay fixture 2026-03-06-session-switch-stale-response-ignore expects only assistant b-a1 but current implementation correctly returns user b-u1 plus assistant; reproduced when trace-replay runs alone.

## Session duplication relation
Separate confirmed issue oqto-9np8: live path/import path split one Pi conversation into raw harness UUID and oqto-* sessions. Store-level fix and unsplit migration exist in current dirty branch but running binaries are explicitly not deployed, matching IMG_8966.

## Remaining acceptance work
- deploy and live-verify single-owner fix + oqto-9np8 fix
- capture Pi/runner/backend/frontend cardinality trace if duplication persists
- add terminal fallback/regression for orphan tool result and stuck spinner
- measure cached chat-switch p50/p95 and optimize to <50 ms
- resolve/correct pre-existing trace fixture expectation, then run full gates

## Architecture constraints
oqto-log remains durable authority; one backend-minted Oqto session id; no text/index/order dedupe; tool pairing by tool_call_id; reload/reconnect parity required.

changes.to:
## Summary
Live chat rendering/upload regressions:
- immediate duplicate streaming deltas corrupt Markdown
- paperclip image upload can spin forever
- tool calls/results can split and spinners can remain active
- active logical session can appear twice in sidebar
- chat switching misses <50 ms target

Screenshots: uploads/IMG_8966.jpeg and uploads/IMG_8967.png.

## Fixes in workspace
1. frontend/lib/ws-manager.ts: one timeline owner per session; replacement subscriptions cannot fan additive deltas out twice; stale unsubscribe cannot remove new owner.
2. frontend/lib/mux-files.ts: HTTP uploads now have a 30-second terminal timeout. XMLHttpRequest previously had its default timeout=0, so a stalled proxy/fileserver request left ChatView isUploading=true and the paperclip spinner active forever. Timeout rejects through the existing try/finally, showing an error toast and restoring the paperclip.

## Regression tests
- frontend/tests/ws-manager-session-owner.test.ts: latest owner gets one delta; stale unsubscribe safety.
- frontend/tests/chat-file-upload.test.ts: stalled upload rejects after configured timeout; successful upload resolves.

## Evidence
PASS: targeted new tests 4/4.
PASS: tool-output-leak 6/6 and tool-summaries 10/10.
PASS: Biome + oxlint on all touched files.
KNOWN PRE-EXISTING/UNRELATED FAILURE: trace-replay fixture 2026-03-06-session-switch-stale-response-ignore expects only assistant b-a1 but implementation returns valid user b-u1 plus assistant; reproduces alone.

## Session duplication relation
Separate confirmed oqto-9np8 identity split. Store fix/migration are in dirty branch but running binaries are not deployed.

## Remaining
- deploy/live verify
- inspect why the upload endpoint stalls (timeout guarantees terminal UX but does not prove backend cause)
- terminal fallback for runtime tool spinners/orphan results
- measure/optimize chat switch <50 ms
- fix trace fixture and run full gates.

changes.from:
Symptom: a session started via one client shows incomplete/divergent chat history when reopened from another machine.

Root cause (evidence, workspace store oqto-log/45661ed61681d8d746e393d4): one pi session (pi UUID 019f5f22-3777-78b7-ab0e-539863fb8232) produced TWO oqto_log_sessions rows for the same conversation:
  1. session_id=platform_id=external_id=019f5f22..., source_kind=pi_agent_end (live streaming path), 12 turns
  2. session_id=platform_id=oqto-1784007500905-e4b1aea20b3398, external_id=019f5f22..., source_kind=pi_jsonl (import path), 13 turns

Live path (oqto-runner/src/pi_manager.rs ~3742) calls append_agent_end_snapshot with session_id AND platform_id both == the raw pi UUID, because pi_manager.rs:3260 `pi_native_id_known = !session_id.starts_with("oqto-")` treats any non-oqto session_id as the pi-native id and never uses a canonical oqto public id. JSONL import path mints oqto-.... Two ingestion paths => two sessions for one conversation => history splits across reload/machines.

Violates ADR-0023 (one public oqto session id; platform_id=Oqto identity, external_id=harness binding; harness ids never become public/join ids) and the sacred session-identity rule.

Fix scope: (1) runner always operates under a minted oqto- id, pi UUID only as external_id, remove starts_with(oqto-) heuristic, fail-closed; (2) trace the start/attach entrypoint that admits a non-oqto session_id; (3) one-time reconciliation of duplicated rows; (4) regression test (one pi session => exactly one oqto_log_session across live+jsonl).

Related: ADR-0023, oqto-zpvs.5, oqto-964n.

--- Prevalence + trigger analysis (2026-07-14) ---
- 70 dual-write splits across this workspace's oqto-log shards (same external_id -> both a raw-UUID and an oqto- session), spanning 2026-01 .. 2026-07-14. Only 1 recent; ~69 Jan-May desktop-era => systemic, not a stale/new PWA.
- Frontend MINTS the id: frontend/lib/session-utils.ts:1880 createPiSessionId() = 'oqto-'+crypto.randomUUID() (secure ctx) else fallback 'oqto-'+Date.now()+'-'+hex. ADR-0023 says BACKEND must mint -> deeper violation.
- Trigger correlation: fallback-format ids (insecure context: http-over-LAN / mobile PWA / webview lacking crypto.randomUUID) are 6% of ALL sessions (137/2187) but 92% of split sessions (65/70) => ~15x enrichment. Today's broken id oqto-1784007500905-e4b1aea20b3398 is fallback format.
- Mitigation (removes trigger, not the class of bug): serve frontend over HTTPS/secure-context so crypto.randomUUID is always present.

--- FIX + UNSPLIT (2026-07-14) ---
FIX (oqto-history): store is now the choke point enforcing ADR-0023 identity.
- store.rs: platform_id_for_external_id() (uuid v5, shared; importer's duplicate copy deleted) + is_canonical_session_id() + canonicalize_session_identity() applied in append_agent_end_snapshot and replace_session_with_snapshot_inner.
- Resolution order: canonical platform_id passes through -> else existing canonical binding for external_id wins (live agent-end + jsonl import converge) -> else pre-existing harness-id session keeps its id (never orphan legacy turns) -> else mint deterministic oqto-{v5}.
- Consistent with ops.rs batch_upsert_session_identities, which already used binding-wins.
- Tests (proven to FAIL without the fix, reproducing the exact prod split):
  one_pi_session_yields_one_oqto_session_across_both_paths, harness_id_alone_mints_a_canonical_identity, existing_harness_id_session_keeps_its_id.

UNSPLIT (new CLI: `oqto runner migrate-oqto-log --mode unsplit|unsplit-dry-run`):
- ops.rs: find_harness_session_splits(), unsplit_harness_sessions() -> UnsplitOutcome, delete_sessions_by_session_id_exact (keys strictly on session_id; delete_session() matches external_id too and would delete the survivor).
- SAFETY: only collapses when the canonical keeper HAS turns. Identity-sync creates canonical rows with 0 turns; for those the harness row is the only copy.

INCIDENT (resolved, no data lost): first migration cut lacked the empty-keeper guard and deleted 11 harness rows whose canonical keeper was empty. Restored all 11 from backup (~/oqto-log-backup-20260714-222140) + FTS rebuild; verified all 69 former splits have content (69 ok / 0 empty / 0 missing).

STATE: 58 splits collapsed; 11 remain, correctly SKIPPED as unsafe (canonical empty).
FOLLOW-UP: the 11 need re-projection from pi JSONL into the canonical keeper (bootstrap mode; with the store fix it now resolves onto the binding), then unsplit collapses them.
NOT DONE: fix not deployed — running oqto/oqto-runner are pre-fix binaries and can still write harness-id rows until rebuilt+restarted.

--- STRENGTHENED: binding wins over a proposed canonical id (2026-07-15) ---
Found a second split source before rebuilding: canonical ids are minted by THREE schemes for the same conversation
  - frontend secure ctx : oqto-{uuid v4}      (1 session)
  - frontend insecure   : oqto-{ms}-{hex}     (137 sessions; the split trigger)

Reported: "in session search is completely broken, doesn't work and when opened results in elements colliding".

TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS.

1) NON-FUNCTIONAL (not a regression — never built).
frontend/lib/api/default-chat.ts:447 searchInPiSession() calls
  GET /api/agents/sessions/{id}/search?q=&limit=
That route DOES NOT EXIST. Proof against the running backend (:8080):
  /api/agents/sessions/test/search -> 200 text/html   (SPA fallback = no route)
  /api/search                      -> 401 application/json (a real route)
  /api/definitely-not-a-route      -> 200 text/html   (identical to the search call)
Only search routes in api/routes.rs are /workspace/memories/search and /search (handlers::search_sessions).

Fails in the worst possible way: the SPA fallback returns HTTP 200, so the client's `if (!res.ok) throw` never fires; it dies inside res.json() parsing "<!doctype html>" -> generic "Search failed" / no results. A 404 would at least be honest.

Root: in-session search was designed for the hstry line-based era (InSessionSearchResult carries `line_number`, which oqto-log has no concept of) and was never ported. oqto-history search_timeline() has TimelineSearchScope { Workdir, Workspace, All } — no Session scope, and TimelineSearchRequest has no session_id field.
Feasible: oqto_log_message_fts already carries session_id (UNINDEXED) [migrations_oqto_log/20260410001_oqto_log_schema_v1.sql:114], so scoping is a WHERE clause. Must match on session_id OR external_id (see oqto-9np8: identity shapes are mixed).

2) LAYOUT COLLISION (real, cheap).
SessionScreen.tsx:1455 renders the header buttons as
  <div className="absolute top-4 right-4 xl:top-6 xl:right-6 flex items-center gap-1 z-10">  (4 buttons)
inside a `relative` parent (line 1386). Each button = p-1.5 + w-4 icon = 28px; 4 buttons + 3x gap-1 = 124px; at right-4 that occupies ~140px from the edge (~148px at xl).
The search bar container (line 1505) reserves only `pr-16` = 64px -> the bar's right-hand controls (result counter, prev/next) render underneath the button cluster.

Also SessionScreen.tsx:1507 passes `sessionId={selectedChatSessionId ?? undefined}` while ChatSearchBarProps declares `sessionId: string | null` — type mismatch.

FIX PLAN
- backend: TimelineSearchScope::Session + session_id on TimelineSearchRequest; filter (s.session_id = ? OR s.external_id = ?); route GET /api/agents/sessions/{id}/search -> handler; tests.
- frontend: drop line_number from InSessionSearchResult (oqto-log has no line numbers; the UI already prefers message_id); fix pr-16 -> clear the ~148px button cluster; fix the ?? undefined.
- consider: unknown /api/* should 404 rather than fall through to the SPA, so dead API calls fail loudly.

Related: oqto-cghp (Expose oqto-log FTS5 query API), oqto-pxve (Search UI overlay), epic oqto-2hyk.

changes.from:
## Outcome

Make Pi approvals and structured user-input requests durable and reconnect-safe so pending interaction can be recovered after frontend reload or transport reconnect, with exactly-once resolution semantics.

## Scope

- Add additive `oqto_log_requests` storage with request id, Oqto session/turn/runtime/item references, request type, pending/resolved/cancelled/expired status, prompt/detail, option/schema payload, response payload, provider/native ref, requested/resolved timestamps, resolver identity, correlation id, and extensions.
- Define typed request states and legal transitions.
- Persist request creation before exposing it to clients.
- Persist resolution transactionally with the command receipt/dedupe key where applicable.
- Rehydrate pending requests on reconnect/reload.
- Reject duplicate, stale, wrong-session, wrong-user, and already-resolved responses with contextual typed errors.
- Handle cancellation when turn/runtime ends without falsely treating it as approval denial.
- Preserve current Pi permission/security semantics; fail closed when durable persistence is unavailable.

## Constraints

- This is security-sensitive: authorization and session identity checks precede resolution.
- Never replay an approval response merely because a UI reconnects.
- Request identity cannot be derived from visible prompt text or list position.
- Do not expose secret values in lifecycle payloads/logs.

## Proof of positive outcome

Integration tests prove:

1. Pending approval survives frontend reload and is shown once.
2. One authorized response resolves it exactly once.
3. Duplicate/stale responses are rejected without invoking Pi twice.
4. Another Account/session cannot resolve it.
5. Runner/WebSocket reconnect does not duplicate or lose the request.
6. Runtime exit cancels outstanding requests with a distinct reason.
7. Restart recovery either safely rebinds a still-actionable native request or fails closed; it never guesses.
8. Audit records identify request, session, resolver, transition, and timestamps without secrets.
9. Existing permission tests and chat behavior continue to pass.

Run security, runner, protocol, history, frontend reconnect, and end-to-end tests warning-free.
changes.to:
## Decision

Removed from the Pi-first oqto-log reliability scope.

Pi does not currently expose a native approval or structured user-input request lifecycle through Oqto's Pi adapter/protocol. Adding durable request storage now would therefore be speculative rather than solving an observed Pi reliability problem.

Create a new issue only when a concrete runtime integration exposes stable request identifiers and lifecycle semantics (for example a future harness adapter, an Oqto security broker, or a Pi extension). Define that schema from real events and prove reconnect/exactly-once behavior against the actual source.

## Explicitly not required by epic oqto-q9sp

- No `oqto_log_requests` table is required for this Pi-first epic.
- Fleet migration work does not depend on this issue.
- Existing secret approval/security broker behavior outside Pi belongs to its own domain issue rather than being attributed to Pi.

changes.from:
## Outcome

Strengthen `oqto-log` as the durable authority for Pi session identity and lifecycle without disrupting existing Pi chat/history behavior, while leaving honest extension seams for future harness adapters.

The work is deliberately staged. Each stage must remain deployable and rollback-compatible. Do not combine the entire epic into one migration or behavior switch.

## Motivation

The current turn-DAG timeline is strong, but session reliability still depends on a single mutable `oqto_log_sessions.external_id`, turn-bound events, and runtime state that is not represented separately from durable session identity. This makes reconnect, resume, fork/import, process restart, approval recovery, and diagnosis harder than necessary.

This epic is valuable with Pi as the only harness. Multi-harness support is a future beneficiary, not the acceptance criterion.

## Architectural constraints

- Preserve ADR-0023: one public Oqto session id; Pi JSONL ids/paths, process ids, RPC ids, and future harness ids are adapter-local bindings only.
- Pi owns its JSONL files; Oqto must never write or mutate them.
- `oqto-log` remains the durable history authority; live runner/control-plane state is a projection, not competing truth.
- Migrations are additive and immutable. Do not edit existing SQL migrations.
- Preserve old binaries/readers during rollout: keep `external_id` as a compatibility projection and dual-write where required.
- Never persist `pending-*` or `tmp:*` ids.
- No reconciliation by message text, visible order, array length, or process id.
- User-owned data is preserve-first: backup/verification and fail-closed migration behavior are mandatory.
- Do not make product behavior depend on new observational records until their accuracy is proven against real traces.

## Delivery sequence

1. Add append-only external session bindings and compatibility backfill.
2. Add runtime-incarnation and session-lifecycle storage.
3. Instrument Pi/runner lifecycle observationally and validate traces.
4. Expose diagnostics/read models only after observational proof.
5. Add durable interactive request lifecycle as an isolated subsystem.
6. Add explicit fleet migration/doctor/deploy safeguards.

## Epic success proof

A reviewer can take a real pre-migration Pi Workspace database, migrate it, and demonstrate:

- all prior sessions, branches, turns, messages, parts, raw envelopes, search results, and projections remain equivalent;
- every non-empty legacy `external_id` has an append-only typed binding;
- a single Oqto session can survive multiple Pi process/runtime incarnations without changing public identity;
- reconnect/resume/process-exit lifecycle events are idempotent and auditable;
- pending approvals/questions recover correctly after frontend reload and reject stale/duplicate responses;
- old-compatible reads still work during staged rollout;
- migration and doctor checks run automatically during deployment and fail closed on integrity violations;
- touched production code passes formatting, linting, unit/integration tests, migration fixtures, and warning-free repository gates.

## Non-goals

- Implement Claude/Codex/OpenCode adapters.
- Replace Pi RPC or the current chat UI.
- Remove `oqto_log_sessions.external_id` in this epic.
- Redefine `turn.role` or rebuild the parts table merely for speculative provider support.
- Store transient terminal attachment or heartbeat state as durable history.
